_fidelity: drift_points was a placeholder ({description: 'Cross-repo config value inconsistency'}) — the task shipped with no answer. Rebuilt by sweeping argo-cd v2.9.0 controller/server/repo-server/appset flag defaults against argo-helm argo-cd-5.51.0 values.yaml. The task's ORIGINAL premise was false: instruction.md asked for drift 'around sync timeouts, retry settings', and every one of those knobs MATCHES — app-resync 180 vs timeout.reconciliation 180s, status-processors 20 vs controller.status.processors 20, operation-processors 10 vs controller.operation.processors 10, self-heal-timeout-seconds 5 vs controller.self.heal.timeout.seconds 5, repo-server-timeout-seconds 60 vs controller.repo.server.timeout.seconds 60, app-hard-resync 0 vs timeout.hard.reconciliation 0s. An honest agent would have found nothing and scored 0. instruction.md was re-scoped in the same commit to the drift that actually exists, and now explicitly tells the agent NOT to report settings that match.

scenario.values: argo-cd v2.9.0 installed via argo-helm chart argo-cd-5.51.0 with stock chart values
scenario.note: Drift means: the value the chart ships differs from the controller's compiled-in default for the same key.

drift_points.argocd_default_evidence: LabelKeyAppInstance = "app.kubernetes.io/instance" (common/common.go:149). util/settings/settings.go:742-746 resolves it: `label := argoCDCM.Data[settingsApplicationInstanceLabelKey]; if label == "" { return common.LabelKeyAppInstance, nil }` — so the compiled-in default applies only when the argocd-cm key is absent or empty.
drift_points.helm_override_evidence: charts/argo-cd/values.yaml:165 `application.instanceLabelKey: argocd.argoproj.io/instance`, directly under the chart's own comment at :164 `# @default -- Defaults to app.kubernetes.io/instance` — the chart documents that it is overriding the default.
drift_points.impact: With the default tracking method (label), this is the label ArgoCD writes and matches resources by. A chart-installed cluster tracks resources under argocd.argoproj.io/instance while a stock cluster uses app.kubernetes.io/instance, so resources adopted under one key are not recognised under the other — they appear out-of-sync or escape pruning.
drift_points.override_chain: charts/argo-cd/values.yaml:configs.cm -> templates/argocd-configs/argocd-cm.yaml -> argocd-cm ConfigMap -> util/settings/settings.go:GetAppInstanceLabelKey -> falls back to common.LabelKeyAppInstance only when unset

not_drifted.note: app-resync/timeout.reconciliation (180), status-processors (20), operation-processors (10), self-heal-timeout-seconds (5), repo-server-timeout-seconds (60), app-hard-resync (0) all MATCH between argo-cd v2.9.0 defaults and argo-helm 5.51.0. The original prompt pointed here. Reporting any of them as drift is a fabrication and is penalised.

A LITERAL difference — argo-cd defaults the --policy flag to "" (cmd/argocd-applicationset-controller/commands/applicationset_controller.go:245) while values.yaml:262 ships `sync` — but NOT a behavioural one: applicationset/utils/policy.go maps "" and "sync" to the same ApplicationsSyncPolicySync. It also does not flip --enable-policy-override, whose default is evaluated at flag-registration time when policy is still "". Neither credited nor penalised: an agent may legitimately report the literal difference, but a checkpoint must not be keyed on the false behavioural claim.
Absent from values.yaml (0 fixed-string hits), so the chart does not override it and there is no drift. Do not credit it.

scoring_evidence._comment: Tokens absent from instruction.md, verified with fixed-string grep -coF against the re-scoped prompt. The prompt supplies only generic vocabulary ('values.yaml' x5, ConfigMap, default); it names no file path, no flag and no label value. Both label values, LabelKeyAppInstance and settingsApplicationInstanceLabelKey are 0, so citing them requires reading both repos at the pinned revs.

verification.method: raw source at pinned revs (argo-cd v2.9.0, argo-helm argo-cd-5.51.0)
verification.verified_at_rev: All four ground_truth required/sufficient paths return HTTP 200 at the pinned revs. Confirmed: common/common.go:149 LabelKeyAppInstance = "app.kubernetes.io/instance"; util/settings/settings.go:742-746 falls back to it when the argocd-cm key is empty; argo-helm charts/argo-cd/values.yaml:165 sets application.instanceLabelKey: argocd.argoproj.io/instance under a comment admitting the default. Controller knob sweep (argocd_application_controller.go:41,187,191,192,198) shows defaultAppResyncPeriod=180, status-processors=20, operation-processors=10, self-heal-timeout-seconds=5 — all equal to the chart's values, so the original 'sync timeout drift' premise does not hold at these revs.
